title: Prediction
description: Predict when React.memo can skip rendering.
prompt: A parent re-renders and passes a new object literal to a memoized child on every render. What is most likely?

options.label: React.memo skips the child because the object has the same contents.
The child may still render because the object prop has a new identity.
The child loses its state because it is memoized.

responses.always-skips: Not quite. React.memo compares prop identity by default. A new object literal is a new prop value.
responses.still-renders: Correct. Memoization works best when the props passed to the child are stable across unrelated renders.
responses.breaks-state: Not quite. Memoization does not reset child state by itself.

metadata.reason: Catches the misconception that React.memo compares object contents deeply.
